guidance_heading: T-SQL dialect rewrite guidance (SQL Server → PostgreSQL)
notes: Migration-pair ruleset for SQL Server 2022 (16.x) → PostgreSQL 18 (second-pair programme, 2026-09-11, shaping doc agent-os/planning/2026-09-11-sqlserver-postgres-pair-shaping.md). Pair knowledge lives HERE as data — generic code never names an engine. Rules with a `comparison` block drive the data-parity and proc-parity comparators; guidance-only rules (comparison: null) carry rewrite/seed knowledge and conventions. Owner rulings bound into this file: CI collation is the estate default (MSPG.COLL.001 enabled); datetime2(7)/time(7) precision loss is a cited rule (MSPG.DT.002); cross-database references and indexed views are OUT by ruling and carry named untranslatable reasons rather than rules.

untranslatable_constructs.concern: Database Mail has no built-in PostgreSQL equivalent (send from the application or an external service)
linked-server / ad-hoc remote queries are cross_database_reference (OUT by ruling)
Service Broker messaging has no database-resident PostgreSQL equivalent (service_broker_object decision)
application locks map to pg_advisory_xact_lock with different key semantics — review
lock hints do not map onto PostgreSQL MVCC semantics (FOR UPDATE / LOCK TABLE review)

token_conversions.note: T-SQL sysutcdatetime() -> Postgres (now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') (100 ns -> microseconds)
T-SQL scope_identity() -> INSERT … RETURNING <id> (or currval(pg_get_serial_sequence())) — decide per call site
T-SQL error_number() -> (PG_EXCEPTION_DETAIL ->> 'source_error')::int inside an EXCEPTION block (MSPG.PROC.ERR.001)
T-SQL error_message() -> SQLERRM inside an EXCEPTION block
T-SQL error_procedure() -> GET STACKED DIAGNOSTICS PG_EXCEPTION_CONTEXT
T-SQL error_line() -> GET STACKED DIAGNOSTICS PG_EXCEPTION_CONTEXT
T-SQL xact_state() has no equivalent: inside an EXCEPTION block the sub-transaction is already rolled back (MSPG.PROC.TXN.001)

untranslatable_reasons.cross_database_reference: references another database or a linked server (OUT by ruling — rewrite in the application or consolidate databases first)
untranslatable_reasons.indexed_view: depends on an indexed (materialised, auto-maintained) view (OUT by ruling)
untranslatable_reasons.clr_object: CLR assembly code has no database-resident equivalent (decision: rewrite_in_app | external_service | drop)
untranslatable_reasons.service_broker_object: Service Broker messaging has no database-resident equivalent (decision: rewrite_in_app | external_service | drop)
untranslatable_reasons.filestream: FILESTREAM storage has no database-resident equivalent (decision: bytea | external_store | drop)

rules.title: SQL Server datetime carries 1/300s precision (.000/.003/.007); Postgres timestamp is microseconds
rules.rewrite_guidance: Map datetime to timestamp(3) (zoneless). Values loaded from SQL Server datetime never carry sub-1/300s precision; the target must not synthesise finer precision on like-for-like paths (getdate() → now() is governed by MSPG.PROC.VOL.001).
rules.scenario_seed: Round-trip a timestamp whose milliseconds are not a multiple of 1/300s and assert the persisted+returned value matches the source rounding (.003/.007).

rules.title: datetime2(7) and time(7) carry 100 ns; Postgres carries microseconds — the 7th digit is lost on load (cited, never silent)
rules.rewrite_guidance: Map datetime2(p) to timestamp(min(p,6)) and time(p) to time(min(p,6)). Columns declared with p = 7 are flagged precision_loss in the pack manifest; the loader TRUNCATES the 7th fractional digit (never rounds) so source and target canonical forms agree; application code that compares datetime2 values for equality across the boundary must compare at microsecond precision.
rules.scenario_seed: Insert a datetime2(7) value with a non-zero 7th digit; assert the migrated value equals the source truncated to microseconds and that ordering/keyset paging over the column is stable.
rules.notes: Comparison canonical form is STRING-based (the wire renders the full fraction): both sides are cut at 6 fractional digits before comparison. Applies equally to datetimeoffset fractions via MSPG.DT.004.

rules.title: smalldatetime has minute precision
rules.rewrite_guidance: Map to timestamp(0); the source rounds to the nearest minute (29.998 s rounds up) — the loader carries the stored minute value verbatim.
rules.scenario_seed: Round-trip a value with seconds and assert minute rounding matches.

rules.title: datetimeoffset compares as an instant (offset-normalised, microsecond precision)
rules.rewrite_guidance: Map datetimeoffset(p) to timestamptz(min(p,6)); the stored instant is preserved but the ORIGINAL offset is not (Postgres normalises to UTC). Application code that reads the offset back (DATEPART(tz, …), SWITCHOFFSET, the offset in FORMAT/CONVERT output) is a flagged rewrite site: carry the offset in a companion smallint column when it is response-visible.
rules.scenario_seed: Store the same instant with two different offsets; assert both read back as the same instant and document that the offset itself is not round-tripped.

rules.title: date compares at day granularity (textual shape differences are not divergence)
rules.rewrite_guidance: Map to date. Style-formatted CONVERT() output (101, 103, 112, 120…) is response-visible and follows the convert construct guidance.
rules.scenario_seed: Round-trip a date and a CONVERT(varchar, date, 112) rendering.

rules.title: SQL Server char/varchar equality ignores trailing spaces (ANSI_PADDING); empty strings are preserved
rules.rewrite_guidance: Postgres compares varchar/text byte-exactly; only char(n) pads. WHERE col = 'x' with trailing-space data diverges — the rewrite right-trims on the comparison side where the application relied on padding-insensitive equality. Unlike Sybase, an empty string stays '' (no single-space coercion).
rules.scenario_seed: Insert 'abc ' and query with 'abc'; assert the same match behaviour. Insert '' and assert it reads back as '' on both engines.

rules.title: nvarchar/nchar/ntext are UTF-16; the target stores UTF-8 (NFC-normalised)
rules.rewrite_guidance: N-typed columns map to varchar/text in a UTF-8 database; supplementary characters (surrogate pairs) are one code point on the target — LEN()/DATALENGTH() arithmetic on UTF-16 units is a flagged rewrite site (use length()/octet_length()).
rules.scenario_seed: Store a string with a supplementary character and a combining sequence; assert equality after NFC normalisation and document the LEN() difference.

rules.title: varchar/char under a code-page collation converts to UTF-8 on load
rules.rewrite_guidance: Non-Unicode columns are decoded with the column's collation code page by the driver and re-encoded as UTF-8; characters the code page could not represent were already lost at the source ('?' substitution) — never a target defect.
rules.scenario_seed: Store an accented character in a varchar column under a Latin1 collation; assert it round-trips as the same code point.

rules.title: SQL Server default collations are case-insensitive (_CI_); Postgres default collations are case-sensitive
rules.rewrite_guidance: The estate default is case-insensitive, so every string equality, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, UNIQUE constraint and JOIN relies on it. Pack-wide decision `collation`: default `citext` for every affected column (keeps LIKE, uniqueness and index behaviour); alternative `icu_nondeterministic` (CREATE COLLATION … provider = icu, locale = 'und-u-ks-level2', deterministic = false — LIKE / regex / pattern operators are NOT supported on such columns); alternative `accept_case_sensitive_change`. The comparator applies case folding only to columns whose source collation contains _CI_ (manifest collation_affected_columns).
rules.scenario_seed: Insert 'ABC' and 'abc' into a UNIQUE column on the source (fails) and assert the target rejects the same; query WHERE name = 'abc' against 'ABC' and assert the same hit.
rules.notes: Owner ruling 2026-09-11: CI default = citext; ICU nondeterministic explicit alternative with its LIKE restriction documented; accept-CS third.

rules.title: money/smallmoney are fixed 4-decimal scale
rules.rewrite_guidance: Map to numeric(19,4)/numeric(10,4); never to floating types. Rounding at scale 4 is part of the observed contract; money arithmetic in T-SQL rounds intermediate results to 4 places.
rules.scenario_seed: Write an amount requiring rounding at the 4th decimal and assert identical rounding behaviour.

rules.title: float/real representational differences across engines
rules.rewrite_guidance: float(n) with n ≤ 24 is real; otherwise double precision. Aggregations over floats may differ in the last ulp; response-visible float formatting (STR(), FORMAT()) is a flagged rewrite site.
rules.scenario_seed: Sum a column of floats and compare within epsilon; render one with STR() and assert the formatted text.

rules.title: numeric/decimal exact-value canonical form
rules.rewrite_guidance: Map numeric(p,s)/decimal(p,s) like-for-like (p ≤ 38 fits Postgres numeric). Both wires carry decimals as strings; trailing-zero scale differences are canonicalised without float parsing.
rules.scenario_seed: Write 123.4500 and assert equality with 123.45 on the canonical form.

rules.title: SQL Server bit is nullable 0/1; Postgres boolean
rules.rewrite_guidance: Map bit to boolean; the loader coerces 0/1 to false/true. Unlike Sybase, a SQL Server bit column CAN be NULL, so NULL is preserved (no default-0 coercion).
rules.scenario_seed: Insert NULL, 0 and 1; assert NULL, false, true on the target.

rules.title: tinyint is unsigned 0..255; Postgres has no unsigned single-byte type
rules.rewrite_guidance: Map to smallint with a CHECK (0..255) so out-of-range writes fail as they did at the source.
rules.scenario_seed: Insert 255 and 256; assert the second fails on both engines.

rules.title: text/ntext/varchar(max)/nvarchar(max) map to text
rules.rewrite_guidance: Map to text. TEXTPTR/WRITETEXT/UPDATETEXT (deprecated) and SUBSTRING over LOBs are rewrite sites; length arithmetic follows MSPG.STR.002.
rules.scenario_seed: Store a > 8000-byte value and assert byte-for-byte equality after NFC.

rules.title: binary/varbinary/image/rowversion byte-exact hex comparison
rules.rewrite_guidance: Map binary types to bytea. `rowversion`/`timestamp` is an auto-incrementing row version, NOT a datetime — a decision (map_to_bytea | drop_column | application_managed) because Postgres has no auto-maintained equivalent (xmin is not stable).
rules.scenario_seed: Round-trip a varbinary with a leading 0x00 byte and assert hex equality.

rules.title: uniqueidentifier compares as a lowercase canonical UUID
rules.rewrite_guidance: Map to uuid (the loader lower-cases the text form). NEWID() → gen_random_uuid(); NEWSEQUENTIALID() has no sequential equivalent (gen_random_uuid() is random — index locality changes, values do not). Byte order differs between the SQL Server binary form and RFC 4122; migrate via the TEXT form only.
rules.scenario_seed: Round-trip a GUID and assert the text forms match case-insensitively; insert through a NEWSEQUENTIALID() default and assert only presence.

rules.title: IDENTITY seed/increment, SCOPE_IDENTITY() and identity caching gaps
rules.rewrite_guidance: IDENTITY(seed, inc) → GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY (START WITH seed INCREMENT BY inc) with the sequence restarted above the source MAX. SCOPE_IDENTITY()/@@IDENTITY/IDENT_CURRENT() → RETURNING id / currval(pg_get_serial_sequence()). SQL Server caches identity values (gaps after restarts) — value gaps are never divergence. SET IDENTITY_INSERT ON → OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE.
rules.scenario_seed: Insert through a trigger that also inserts; assert the application observes the same id (SCOPE_IDENTITY vs @@IDENTITY semantics).

rules.title: xml columns compare after whitespace canonicalisation
rules.rewrite_guidance: Map to xml. SQL Server stores XML as a parsed binary form and re-serialises it (attribute order and insignificant whitespace may differ from the input); Postgres stores the text. Typed XML (schema collections) loses validation — flagged.
rules.scenario_seed: Store an XML document with insignificant whitespace and assert canonical equality.

rules.title: XML methods (.value(), .query(), .nodes(), .exist(), .modify()) are rewrite sites
rules.rewrite_guidance: .value('xpath', 'type') → (xpath('xpath/text()', col))[1]::type; .exist() → xpath_exists(); .nodes() → xmltable(); .query() → xpath() array; .modify() has no equivalent — rebuild the document. OPENXML → xmltable. FOR XML PATH/AUTO/RAW → xmlagg/xmlelement (or string_agg for the ‘concatenation’ idiom).
rules.scenario_seed: Drive each XML-method site with a representative document and compare the extracted values.

rules.title: sql_variant has no Postgres equivalent
rules.rewrite_guidance: Pack decision sql_variant_column: default jsonb ({"type": <base type>, "value": <text>}), alternatives text (value only, type lost) and drop_column. SQL_VARIANT_PROPERTY() reads → jsonb accessors.
rules.scenario_seed: Store an int, a string and a datetime in one sql_variant column; assert type + value survive in the jsonb form.

rules.title: hierarchyid maps to ltree (string form)
rules.rewrite_guidance: Extract with col.ToString() ('/1/2/'); map to ltree (extension) with '/'-paths converted to '.'-labels (decision hierarchyid_column: ltree default | text). GetAncestor/GetDescendant/IsDescendantOf/GetLevel → ltree operators (subpath, @>, <@, nlevel).
rules.scenario_seed: Store a three-level path and assert ancestor/descendant queries return the same rows.

rules.title: geography/geometry map to PostGIS types; compared as WKT
rules.rewrite_guidance: Extract as WKT (col.STAsText()) with SRID (col.STSrid); load as ST_GeomFromText(wkt, srid). PostGIS must be installed on the target (pack runbook prerequisite). STDistance/STIntersects/STArea → ST_Distance/ST_Intersects/ST_Area. Decision spatial_column: postgis default | wkt_text | drop_column.
rules.scenario_seed: Store a polygon and a point; assert STIntersects and ST_Intersects agree.

rules.title: System-versioned temporal tables are emulated with a history table and a versioning trigger

convention.history_table: <schema>.<table>_history with the base columns plus valid_from/valid_to timestamptz
convention.trigger: haikai_temporal_versioning() AFTER UPDATE OR DELETE copies the OLD row into the history table with valid_to = clock_timestamp()
convention.for_system_time_rewrite: FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF t → base rows UNION ALL history rows WHERE valid_from <= t AND valid_to > t; BETWEEN/FROM/CONTAINED IN → the equivalent range predicates; ALL → base UNION ALL history

rules.rewrite_guidance: Pack decision temporal_table: emulate_history_table (default) | drop_history | application_managed. Period columns (GENERATED ALWAYS AS ROW START/END) become valid_from/valid_to maintained by the trigger. The source history table is loaded into the emulated history table.
rules.scenario_seed: Update a row twice and query FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF the midpoint; assert the same historical version is returned.

rules.title: Full-text indexes are emulated with tsvector + GIN; CONTAINS/FREETEXT are rewrite sites
rules.rewrite_guidance: Pack decision fulltext_index: tsvector_gin (default: generated tsvector column + GIN index) | drop_index. CONTAINS(col, 'a AND b') → col_tsv @@ to_tsquery('a & b'); FREETEXT → plainto_tsquery / websearch_to_tsquery; CONTAINSTABLE/FREETEXTTABLE rank → ts_rank. Ranking and stemming differ — results are compared as sets with an advisory note on order.
rules.scenario_seed: Run a CONTAINS query with an AND and a prefix term; assert the same row set (order advisory).

rules.title: Shape-adaptive calling convention for translated procedures and functions

convention.function_name: routine name, lower case, in the mapped target schema
convention.arg_naming: source parameter name without the @ sigil, lower case, source order
convention.out_param_naming: same as arg_naming; OUTPUT parameters become OUT arguments
convention.table_valued_params: READONLY table-type parameters become arguments of the emitted composite type array (<type>[]); the caller passes an array literal or unnests

shapes.return_status: no result set, no OUTPUT parameter: RETURNS integer (the RETURN value; 0 when the source returns nothing)
shapes.single_result_set: exactly one result-producing SELECT and a trivial return status: RETURNS TABLE(<columns of that SELECT>) / SETOF; the existing {call}+executeQuery JDBC pattern keeps working
shapes.out_params: OUTPUT parameters and no result set: OUT arguments (plus OUT return_status when the status is non-trivial); the registered-parameter JDBC pattern keeps working
shapes.rich: more than one result set, or a result set combined with OUTPUT parameters or a non-trivial return status: OUT refcursor arguments rs1..rsN in source order + OUT return_status + OUT parameters; the caller must run inside a transaction and FETCH ALL from each cursor
shapes.table_function: inline and multi-statement table-valued functions: RETURNS TABLE(<columns>) — called as SELECT * FROM f(...) exactly as on the source
shapes.scalar_function: scalar user-defined functions: RETURNS <mapped type>; called as SELECT f(...) exactly as on the source

convention.selection: table_function for TVFs and scalar_function for scalar UDFs; else rich when max_result_sets > 1 or (max_result_sets == 1 and (has_output_params or not return_status_trivial)); single_result_set when max_result_sets == 1; out_params when has_output_params; otherwise return_status

rules.rewrite_guidance: Emit EXACTLY the header the descriptor prescribes (name, argument names/order/types, OUT arguments, RETURNS clause). Keep every ORDER BY. Lower-case unquoted identifiers. Never add behaviour the source lacks.
rules.scenario_seed: Invoke through the descriptor's shape on the target and compare the full envelope (return status, OUT values, every result set, messages, state delta) against the captured baseline.

rules.title: RAISERROR and THROW carry their source error number, severity and state through a fixed SQLSTATE

convention.raise_form: RAISE EXCEPTION USING ERRCODE = 'P0001', MESSAGE = <text>, DETAIL = '{"source_error": <n>, "severity": <s>, "state": <st>}'
convention.throw_numbers: THROW n, msg, state carries n verbatim (user numbers are >= 50000); RAISERROR('text', sev, state) without a number carries 50000; sys.messages ids (RAISERROR(50001, …)) carry the id
convention.rethrow: a bare THROW inside CATCH becomes RAISE; (re-raise the caught exception unchanged)
convention.error_functions: ERROR_NUMBER() → (PG_EXCEPTION_DETAIL ->> 'source_error')::int, ERROR_MESSAGE() → SQLERRM, ERROR_SEVERITY()/ERROR_STATE() → DETAIL keys, ERROR_PROCEDURE()/ERROR_LINE() → GET STACKED DIAGNOSTICS PG_EXCEPTION_CONTEXT
convention.engine_errors: engine-raised errors (547 FK, 2627/2601 unique, 515 not-null, 8152 truncation, 245/8114 conversion) map onto the Postgres SQLSTATE class (23503, 23505, 23502, 22001, 22P02) — the comparator matches error FAMILY for engine errors and source_error for user errors

rules.rewrite_guidance: Every RAISERROR/THROW becomes RAISE EXCEPTION with SQLSTATE P0001 and a DETAIL JSON carrying the source number/severity/state; the message text is carried verbatim (RAISERROR printf-style %s/%d substitution is rendered with format()). Never map business errors onto engine SQLSTATEs.
rules.scenario_seed: Drive each RAISERROR/THROW site and assert the same source error number surfaces on both engines; drive a constraint violation and assert the same error family.

rules.title: PRINT and informational messages become RAISE NOTICE and are advisory in comparison
rules.rewrite_guidance: PRINT <text> becomes RAISE NOTICE '%', <text>; RAISERROR(..., 0..10, ...) WITH NOWAIT (informational severities) also becomes RAISE NOTICE. Message text differences never fail a comparison on their own.
rules.scenario_seed: Drive a PRINT path and confirm the notice is captured on both sides.

rules.title: Result-set rows compare ordered only when the producing SELECT carries ORDER BY
rules.rewrite_guidance: Keep every ORDER BY exactly (including OFFSET … FETCH → OFFSET … LIMIT); never add one the source lacks. TOP without ORDER BY is engine-dependent and compared as a multiset.
rules.scenario_seed: Drive a result set whose SELECT has no ORDER BY and confirm the multiset comparison; drive one with ORDER BY on a tie and confirm the tiebreak.

rules.title: Result-set column names compare case-insensitively; translations emit lower-case unquoted names
rules.rewrite_guidance: Emit lower-case, unquoted column aliases matching the source select list ([Bracketed Alias] → bracketed_alias with spaces replaced by underscores, noted); pgjdbc column lookup is case-insensitive so DB-only call sites keep working.
rules.scenario_seed: Confirm every source column name is present (case-insensitively) and in the same position.

rules.title: Result-set and OUT-parameter cells compare under the column-type rules via a driver-type map
rules.rewrite_guidance: Not a rewrite rule: the comparator maps each engine's reported cell type onto the ruleset column-type vocabulary so DT/STR/NUM/BIT/BIN/UUID/XML rules apply to envelope cells exactly as to table cells. NOTE: the Postgres driver token `timestamp` maps to datetime2 (microsecond family), never to the 1/300 s datetime family.
rules.scenario_seed: n/a

rules.title: TRY/CATCH, XACT_ABORT, nested transactions and statement-level error continuation

convention.try_catch: BEGIN TRY … END TRY BEGIN CATCH … END CATCH → BEGIN … EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN … END with GET STACKED DIAGNOSTICS for the ERROR_* functions (MSPG.PROC.ERR.001)
convention.xact_abort_on: SET XACT_ABORT ON = whole-routine abort on error = the Postgres default; no extra structure
convention.xact_abort_off_continuation: SET XACT_ABORT OFF (the default) with a fallible statement followed by further statements and no enclosing TRY/CATCH or @@ERROR check (profile construct error_continuation) → each such statement is wrapped in its own BEGIN … EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN <record the error into a local @@ERROR-equivalent> END sub-block carrying the comment '-- MSPG.PROC.TXN.001 continue-after-error', so the routine continues exactly as the source did (like-for-like; capture evidence is the oracle)
convention.nested_begin_tran: BEGIN TRAN inside a routine with @@TRANCOUNT > 0 → SAVEPOINT; COMMIT at depth > 1 → RELEASE SAVEPOINT; ROLLBACK TRAN → ROLLBACK (aborts the whole transaction, as the source does); ROLLBACK TRAN <savepoint> → ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT
convention.outermost_commit: an outermost COMMIT inside a PROCEDURE is allowed (CALL outside a transaction block); inside a FUNCTION it cannot exist — the translator emits RAISE EXCEPTION USING ERRCODE = 'P0002', MESSAGE = 'source routine committed inside a function' only when the source shape is a function, otherwise the routine is emitted as a PROCEDURE
convention.trancount_reads: @@TRANCOUNT reads → a local depth counter maintained by the emitted savepoint sub-blocks (1 when called inside a transaction)
convention.inner_rollback: RAISE EXCEPTION USING ERRCODE = 'P0002', MESSAGE = 'source routine rolled back' when the source ROLLBACK aborts the caller's transaction

rules.rewrite_guidance: Preserve the observed error and transaction behaviour like-for-like: error-continuation paths are reproduced with per-statement sub-blocks, TRY/CATCH becomes an EXCEPTION block, XACT_ABORT ON needs nothing, nested transactions become savepoints. Never emit COMMIT/ROLLBACK inside a function body.
rules.scenario_seed: Drive a constraint violation on the first fallible write and assert whether the following statements ran (continue-after-error) or not, and assert the caller's transaction state matches; drive the inner-rollback path.

rules.title: Clock-derived cells are volatility: compared as non-null timestamps within the run window
rules.rewrite_guidance: getdate()/sysdatetime() → now() (statement start) or clock_timestamp() (per call); getutcdate()/sysutcdatetime() → (now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'); sysdatetimeoffset() → now() (timestamptz). The comparator never asserts equality of clock values captured at different wall times.
rules.scenario_seed: Capture a clock-bearing result twice and confirm the volatility evidence marks the cell.

rules.title: Random / generated-id cells are volatility: compared by presence only
rules.rewrite_guidance: newid()/newsequentialid() → gen_random_uuid(); rand() → random(); crypt_gen_random(n) → gen_random_bytes(n) (pgcrypto). Values are never asserted equal.
rules.scenario_seed: Confirm the cell is non-null on both sides.

rules.title: Capture connections apply the application driver's session defaults explicitly

set: set transaction isolation level read committed

rules.rewrite_guidance: These are the SQL Server client-library defaults (mssql-jdbc / ODBC / .NET) — closer to Postgres semantics than Sybase's (ANSI nulls ON, NULL-propagating concatenation). Behaviour that depends on a session option (ANSI_NULLS OFF procs, ARITHABORT, CONCAT_NULL_YIELDS_NULL OFF) is reproduced explicitly on the target; procs compiled with SET ANSI_NULLS OFF carry that fact in their profile.
rules.scenario_seed: n/a — the profile is applied on every capture connection and recorded in the envelope.
rules.notes: PROC_CALL_SESSION_SET overrides the list (semicolon-separated). Numeric isolation levels are NOT valid on SQL Server; the named form is used.

rules.title: Statement-level triggers over inserted/deleted map to transition tables; INSTEAD OF on views is row-level; ordering and recursion are explicit

convention.inserted_deleted: CREATE TRIGGER … AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON <table> REFERENCING NEW TABLE AS inserted OLD TABLE AS deleted FOR EACH STATEMENT EXECUTE FUNCTION <fn>(); the body reads inserted/deleted exactly as the source did
convention.per_event_branches: IF UPDATE(col) / COLUMNS_UPDATED() branches use TG_OP and compare inserted vs deleted columns over the transition tables
convention.instead_of_view: INSTEAD OF triggers on views become row-level (FOR EACH ROW) INSTEAD OF triggers using NEW/OLD; note instead_of_row_level
convention.instead_of_table: INSTEAD OF triggers on tables are a decision (instead_of_table_trigger): default before_trigger_emulation (BEFORE trigger that performs the source logic and RETURNs NULL to suppress the original write) | rewrite_in_app
convention.disabled: a disabled source trigger is emitted then ALTER TABLE … DISABLE TRIGGER
convention.ordering: sp_settriggerorder first/last become a_/z_ name prefixes (PostgreSQL fires same-event triggers alphabetically), noted in the manifest
convention.recursion: a trigger that writes its own table is a trigger_recursion decision (SQL Server RECURSIVE_TRIGGERS is OFF by default; PostgreSQL re-fires unconditionally)
convention.nocount_rowcount: SET NOCOUNT ON inside a trigger is dropped; @@ROWCOUNT at trigger start -> the transition-table row count

rules.rewrite_guidance: Translate triggers statement-level with transition tables; never collapse a multi-row source trigger into a row-level one; INSTEAD OF on views is the one row-level shape.
rules.scenario_seed: Fire a multi-row UPDATE through the trigger and assert the same downstream rows on both engines; fire an INSTEAD OF view insert and assert the base-table rows.

rules.title: JDBC call-pattern compatibility per target shape

return_status.exec_text: needs_change: EXEC text is T-SQL; call SELECT <function>() instead
return_status.error_number_branching: needs_change: SQL Server error numbers arrive in SQLSTATE P0001 DETAIL (user errors) or as a Postgres SQLSTATE family (engine errors), not SQLServerException.getErrorCode()

single_result_set.jdbc_call_return: needs_change: a set-returning function has no return value; drop the ? = and read the result set
single_result_set.exec_text: needs_change: EXEC text is T-SQL; SELECT * FROM <function>(...) instead
single_result_set.error_number_branching: needs_change: SQL Server error numbers arrive in SQLSTATE P0001 DETAIL (user errors) or as a Postgres SQLSTATE family (engine errors), not SQLServerException.getErrorCode()

out_params.jdbc_call_return: needs_change: the return status is an OUT argument named return_status, not the ? = slot
out_params.exec_text: needs_change: EXEC text is T-SQL; SELECT * FROM <function>(...) instead
out_params.error_number_branching: needs_change: SQL Server error numbers arrive in SQLSTATE P0001 DETAIL (user errors) or as a Postgres SQLSTATE family (engine errors), not SQLServerException.getErrorCode()

rich.jdbc_call_return: needs_change: refcursor shape — run inside a transaction and register OUT cursor parameters (Types.REF_CURSOR)
rich.jdbc_call: needs_change: refcursor shape — run inside a transaction and register OUT cursor parameters (Types.REF_CURSOR)
rich.exec_text: needs_change: refcursor shape — run inside a transaction and register OUT cursor parameters (Types.REF_CURSOR)
rich.bare_reference: needs_change: refcursor shape — run inside a transaction and register OUT cursor parameters (Types.REF_CURSOR)
rich.error_number_branching: needs_change: SQL Server error numbers arrive in SQLSTATE P0001 DETAIL (user errors) or as a Postgres SQLSTATE family (engine errors), not SQLServerException.getErrorCode()

table_function.jdbc_call_return: needs_change: a table-valued function is queried with SELECT * FROM f(...), not called
table_function.jdbc_call: needs_change: a table-valued function is queried with SELECT * FROM f(...), not called
table_function.exec_text: compatible: SELECT * FROM f(...) text is the same on both engines
table_function.error_number_branching: needs_change: SQL Server error numbers arrive in SQLSTATE P0001 DETAIL (user errors) or as a Postgres SQLSTATE family (engine errors), not SQLServerException.getErrorCode()

scalar_function.exec_text: compatible: SELECT f(...) text is the same on both engines
scalar_function.error_number_branching: needs_change: SQL Server error numbers arrive in SQLSTATE P0001 DETAIL (user errors) or as a Postgres SQLSTATE family (engine errors), not SQLServerException.getErrorCode()

rules.rewrite_guidance: Service-plane rewrites read the per-routine descriptor and this matrix; call sites classified compatible keep their code, needs_change sites carry the named change. Code branching on SQLServerException.getErrorCode() (547, 2627, 2601, 50000+) is a flagged call site.
rules.scenario_seed: n/a — deterministic classification of code-scan call sites.

construct_refs.seed: Freeze/inject clock or mark timestamp fields volatile; getdate() precision follows MSPG.DT.001, sysdatetime() follows MSPG.DT.002.
Probe NULL-argument paths: isnull(x,y) typing follows the FIRST arg in T-SQL, coalesce follows the highest type — seed a scenario where the types differ.

Seed each convert() style code in use — date style codes (101, 103, 112, 120, 121, 126, 127) have no direct to_char equivalent and formatting is response-visible; TRY_CONVERT returns NULL instead of raising.
Seed an insert-through-trigger path: @@identity sees the LAST identity including triggers, SCOPE_IDENTITY() the current scope; the rewrite must preserve which id the app observed.
Seed an update-zero-rows path; branch logic on @@rowcount must behave identically (GET DIAGNOSTICS row_count).
Seed a constraint-violation path; vendor error-code branching must map to the equivalent condition, and the API-visible error body is part of the oracle.
Seed the CATCH path with a constraint violation AND a user THROW; assert ERROR_NUMBER()/ERROR_MESSAGE() derived values and whether the transaction remained committable (XACT_STATE).
Seed every THROW site (user number ≥ 50000) and a bare re-THROW inside CATCH; assert the same source error number surfaces.
Seed an error under SET XACT_ABORT ON and OFF; assert whether subsequent statements ran and whether the transaction was rolled back.
Seed a failing statement that the source silently continues past; assert the following statements' effects are present on both engines (like-for-like).
Call the routine inside and outside an outer transaction; assert @@TRANCOUNT-dependent branches behave the same.
Seed a partial rollback to a savepoint and assert only the inner work is undone.
Seed MERGE with matched/not-matched/not-matched-by-source branches and OUTPUT; assert row effects (PG 15+ MERGE; NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE needs PG 17+).
Seed OUTPUT INSERTED.*/DELETED.* into a table variable and as a result set; assert the same rows are returned (RETURNING / CTE).
Seed a table-variable path with > 1 row; scoping and statistics differences never change results — assert equality.
Seed a READONLY table-valued parameter call with 0, 1 and many rows.
Seed OFFSET … FETCH on a tie; without a deterministic ORDER BY the page contents may legitimately differ.
Seed CROSS/OUTER APPLY over a TVF (→ LATERAL); assert row multiplicity.
Seed IIF with a NULL condition (→ CASE).
Seed TRY_CONVERT/TRY_CAST with an unconvertible value; assert NULL is produced, not an error.
Seed STRING_AGG with WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY …) and with NULL elements.
Seed parameterised dynamic SQL (sp_executesql @stmt, @params, …) including an OUTPUT parameter (→ EXECUTE … USING / INTO).
Seed NEXT VALUE FOR in an INSERT and in a SELECT; assert monotonic values (nextval).
Seed FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF / BETWEEN over the emulated history table (MSPG.TEMPORAL.001).
Seed CONTAINS/FREETEXT with AND, OR and prefix terms (MSPG.FULLTEXT.001) — row set compared, order advisory.
Seed each .value()/.query()/.nodes()/.exist() site with a representative document (MSPG.XML.002).
Seed a TOP-n / TOP (n) PERCENT / WITH TIES query on a tie: without a deterministic ORDER BY tiebreak the selected rows may legitimately differ.
Concurrency detour: lock-hint semantics do not map onto MVCC; seed a two-session scenario if the estate relies on blocking reads (→ SELECT … FOR UPDATE).
NOLOCK dirty reads have no MVCC equivalent; the like-for-like target reads committed data — seed only to document the intentional divergence.
Seed the proc paths using #temp tables end-to-end; scoping and implicit creation semantics differ (CREATE TEMP TABLE … ON COMMIT DROP).
Seed the error path: raiserror severity/message formatting (printf %s/%d) is response-visible where procs surface errors to the API.
SET ROWCOUNT limits DML in T-SQL (deprecated for DML on SQL Server); seed the affected update path — silent partial updates are a data-integrity trap.
Seed SCOPE_IDENTITY() after an insert that fires a trigger inserting elsewhere; assert the id the application observed.
OUT by ruling: routines referencing another database or a linked server carry the named reason cross_database_reference and are not attempted.
